question: What is the 40-byte region at ObjectRegistry +0x70..0x98, and what is the complete lock discipline of the registry's two mutexes?
answer: The region is the registry's second std::mutex, objects_mutex_ (40-byte pthread_mutex_t, guards the +0x30 managed_objects_ map). The +0x98 mutex is library_mutex_ (guards libraries_). objects_mutex_ is never locked, read, written or destroyed by any code in this binary; the managed-object methods that would lock it are absent.

IDENTIFIED (was #4015's open unknown): 40-byte pthread_mutex_t; zeroed by the ctor and the clone with the same 16+16+8 pattern as the +0x98 mutex; never locked, read or written by any registry routine; never destroyed; guards the +0x30 map per the upstream source

IDENTIFIED: 40-byte pthread_mutex_t; zeroed like objects_mutex_; locked by exactly the three libraries_-mutating routines (AddLibrary, big registry method, TTL registration); never destroyed; guards libraries_ per the upstream source

objects_mutex.note: Zero-initialized, never used. The managed-object methods that would lock it (SetManagedObject, GetManagedObject, ListManagedObjects) are absent from this binary: no 'Object already exists: ' string, no 'Registered Plugins:' string, no disp-0x70 lock in any registry-referencing FDE. The binary's only 'managed' string (file offset 0x95f620) is the unrelated RocksDB iterator error 'Managed iterator is not supported anymore.'.

library_mutex.note: Locked by exactly three routines, all of which mutate libraries_: AddLibrary, the big registry method 0x5ff88c0, the TTL registration. Each locks then unlocks around the vector append.

lock_census.note: The 8 disp-0x70 sites (5 lock, 3 unlock) sit in 5 FDEs, all other classes' mutexes (see foreign_lock70). The 28 disp-0x98 sites include the 6 registry sites (3 lock + 3 unlock) and 22 other classes' +0x98 mutexes (ObjectLibrary mu_ and Env/Statistics-area mutexes); none of the 22 is in a registry-marked FDE.

destroy_census.note: The binary's only pthread_mutex_destroy call is inside helper 0x60d5170. Its 74 callers never pass a +0x70 or +0x98 displacement, and none is in a registry-marked FDE. The registry dispose 0x61f8760 never calls the helper (verified in its excerpt): neither registry mutex is ever destroyed.

init_census.note: No pthread_mutex_init targets a registry mutex: both registry mutexes are zero-initialized by the ctor/clone instead.

source_corroboration.note: The member names and guard roles come from the upstream object_registry.cc, which is stable across the bracketing versions: RocksDB 7.8.3 (electrs-librocksdb-sys 0.9.0-e3+7.8.3) and 9.10.0 (ckb-librocksdb-sys 9.10.0) both show objects_mutex_ guarding managed_objects_ and library_mutex_ guarding libraries_. The 8.1.1 header 404s on raw.githubusercontent.com, so the 8.1.1 declaration order itself is not directly confirmed; the binary identification rests on size (40 = pthread_mutex_t), identical zeroing, identical dispose treatment, the +0x98 lockers proving library_mutex_, and elimination for +0x70.

sole_managed_string.text: Managed iterator is not supported anymore.
sole_managed_string.note: The binary's only case-insensitive 'managed' string is this unrelated RocksDB iterator error message; it has nothing to do with the registry's managed-object API.

relocations.note: The vtable-region rows re-ship #4015's 20 RELATIVE records plus the 4 R_X86_64_64 typeinfo-pointer records in the same span.

corrections_to_4015: The +0x70..0x98 region is objects_mutex_, a second std::mutex (40-byte pthread_mutex_t) -- not 'possibly a second mutex or plain data'.
The +0x98 field is library_mutex_, the mutex guarding libraries_ -- its locker set is exactly AddLibrary, the big registry method 0x5ff88c0, and the TTL registration.
The +0x30 map is managed_objects_ (map<string, weak_ptr<Customizable>>), guarded by objects_mutex_.
The +0x18 vector's upstream name is plugins_ (vector<string>); the binary shows AddLibrary appending the name there.
Neither mutex is destroyed: the dispose never calls the mutex-destructor helper, and the binary's only pthread_mutex_destroy site is elsewhere.
open_unknowns: The 8.1.1 header itself was not read (404 on the raw URL); the member names rest on the 7.8.3/9.10.0 bracket plus binary elimination.
Whether the managed-object methods exist in the 8.1.1 source but were stripped at link time, or were never referenced: the binary cannot distinguish these.
The exact identities of the five +0x70-locking classes (named by code area only).

A hypothetical free function taking the registry as its second argument and locking +0x98 would escape the registry-marker filter; no such function exists in the upstream source (all locking sites are methods), so this is a source-backed exclusion, not a binary proof.
